name: Larry
description: Fifty-something, built like he used to do something physical and stopped. Larry has a mustache that belongs to a different decade and eyes that have seen the Mouse Trap empty and the Mouse Trap less empty, and that's the full range. He stands behind the bar like he's waiting for something that already happened. His shirt is always flannel. The color changes. The flannel does not.
habit: Wipes the same spot on the bar in slow circles. Not because it's dirty. Because his hands need something to do while the room is empty. Which is always.
voice: Minimal. 'Yep.' 'Nope.' 'What'll it be.' Larry doesn't start conversations. If you start one, he'll participate the way a wall participates in a game of catch — he's there, but he's not throwing anything back.
want: Quiet. Larry has it. The Mouse Trap gives him exactly the amount of human contact he can tolerate, which is almost none. This is not loneliness. This is preference.
fear: A crowd. Not a dangerous crowd — just a crowd. More than six people in the Mouse Trap and Larry's whole system breaks down. He doesn't know how to be busy. He's never had to learn.
